priorRawFrames: The existing dedicated and LAN reports contain server timings, GUI inputs and screenshots. A workspace search found no raw per-frame time series for these loaded native hulls.
topology: Separate fresh singleplayer saves, one full rendered client with its integrated server on an isolated Windows desktop, no LAN guest, survival, cheats disabled. Other tests shared the host, including the ongoing orbital soak. Only one integrated-flight JVM ran at once.
preparation: Each save reopens the genuine original Advanced Rocketry large-dock manifest for that length. QA supplies energy and oxygen equipment, teleports the host onto the loaded ship and records a prepared home berth. The pilot opens the bridge to choose the Moon, then uses the paired terminal on the lunar deck for return. Initial assembly, normal material collection and wide multi-deck ship geometries are outside these trips.
measurement: Wall-clock time from one Forge client RenderTickEvent.END to the next consecutive render-thread frame, including time waiting for work and the display. Each interval is assigned to its starting phase; both phase labels, both dimension keys and both GUI names are retained in the raw CSV. Nearest-rank percentiles. All intervals within the ship phases are included, with the totals reflecting frame counts per phase. The final screenshot was taken only after the raw stream was closed. Time is frame cadence, not isolated GPU execution time.
interpretation: Each length had a functional round trip with independently measured support at both endpoints. The phase results must be used to assess smoothness: few very slow return frames can consume more wall time than numerous faster outbound frames.

returnPerformanceFix.originals: AR + LibVulpes + Galacticraft Core and the original shipyard bridge. These frame benchmarks did not install ExtraPlanets or GalaxySpace.

profile.method: 100-block baseline, sampled render and integrated-server thread stacks nominally every 19 ms. Independent counters time OrbitScreen draws and wire serialization. Sampling is observational; sample fractions are not exact CPU percentages.

returnPerformanceFix.change: Only the locked Retrofit 0.6.2-beta Galacticraft moonblock ID uses its original hasTileEntity(metadata) to mark states without an original tile as non-ticking. Unrelated blocks and states with a tile use the normal library path.
returnPerformanceFix.baselineMethod: Current ForgeGradle reobf production mixin and config on the pre-fix ship benchmark JAR. Separate fresh survival saves with equal manifests, display settings, machine inventories and flight inputs. JAR digests per run. At least one other soak or test used this PC.

otherAttempts.result: Profile-on candidate reached home, the captain fell, and the 3 GiB heap was exhausted while saving distant chunks. Timed out.
First 300-block candidate reached home. A server thread dump caught a fall-check ray waiting for distant chunks. Captain death followed.

The second 300-block trial fell at the correct home X/Z, 149 blocks below the intended deck. The saved pilot had zero health and the paid ledger still recorded the undelivered captain. No ray over 64 blocks was observed in this run.
The QA listener chose IPv6. The IPv4 guest could not join.
Two TCP/integrated clients arrived on the Moon. The QA observer used an unmapped inherited method while measuring the visitor. An explicit vanilla owner corrected the fixture.

Both clients crossed both dimensions. Before delivery the captain and visitor acquired speed of 19931.48 blocks per tick. The diagnostic stopped the impossible fall ray at the captain rather than generating its terrain. The VS dragging vector and raw moves are archived.

returnPerformanceFix.coverage: Prepared cargo trips use real rendered clients on the test PC and GUI-driven pilot actions. The LAN visitor stays aboard. The measurement covers the stated narrow hulls and the tested hardware. Dungeon observation checks the ticking original skeleton-boss spawner with no player in the room.

arrivalPhysics.scope: Separate physical handoff failure, observed with only the lunar-ticker fix. The GUI pilot could enter the destination while the pending passenger was still falling. At 300 blocks, one disk save showed zero health on terrain at the correct X/Z, roughly 149 blocks below the deck.
arrivalPhysics.capture: 100-block LAN, two full clients. The captain had 21.8335 blocks of accumulated fall distance with a server motion of (0,0,19931.4834054). The recorded VS last-frame ship movement was roughly (-19760,-27.77,-19930). The fixture stopped before traversing the ray. See run-100-lanfix3.
arrivalPhysics.experiment: At a Starbridge native dimensional transfer, advance the destination native ShipData history to the newly installed transform before transferring riders. VS 2.4.11 exposes updatePrevTickShipTransform(), which copies the current transform into the previous-tick field used by EntityDragger. Vehicle physics and ordinary fall damage remain active in the experiment.
arrivalPhysics.clientTest: 100-block LAN trip on the separately identified prototype candidate. Both clients visited the original Moon and home, with independent standing and save checks.

verifiedProduction.conditions: Separate saves on one machine. The 300/200 sequence and 100 LAN/solo sequence ran in parallel during parts of these trials, in addition to other background tests. The 100/200/300 hulls are identically 7 wide and 6 tall, measured with the original Advanced Rocketry construction manifest, Galacticraft Moon and pre-provisioned cargo and equipment.
